messages.text: Actually, it follows the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, and is referring to a case where the firstborn donkey is worth only a shekel, the same value as a lamb suitable for redemption, in which case there is no difference between the value of the donkey and that of the lamb. And Rabbi Yehuda holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda that one may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a lamb that is less than the value of a shekel, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: סלע דהשתא ליכא ביני ביני דההוא שה דיהבינן לכהן תותיה בעי למיהוי שוה שקל:
notes.en: That is worth only a shekel: a sela. For now there is no difference, since the lamb we give the priest in its place must be worth a shekel.

notes.he: אמר רבה לעולם ר' יהודה ואמאי תני אינה מקודשת כגון שאינו שוה הפטר חמור אלא שקל וסבר לה ר' יהודה כר' יוסי בר יהודה דתניא תפדה בשה תפדה מיד אפילו קודם ל' תפדה כל שהוא כלומר אפילו בשה כל דהוא שאינו שוה אלא זוז:
notes.en: Rabba said [the Davidson English reads: Rabba bar Avuh says that Rav says]: actually it is Rabbi Yehuda; and why does it teach that she is not betrothed? Where the firstborn donkey is worth only a shekel, and Rabbi Yehuda holds like Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, as it is taught: “You shall redeem with a lamb”: you shall redeem immediately, even before thirty [days]; you shall redeem with any amount, that is, even with any lamb at all, worth only a zuz.

messages.text: When the Torah states: “You shall redeem,” with regard to a firstborn donkey, it teaches that you shall redeem it immediately, and you shall redeem it for any amount.

notes.he: תרי זמני כתיב ופטר חמור תפדה בשה (שמות י״ג:י״ג):
notes.en: “You shall redeem,” “you shall redeem”: it is written twice: “And every firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 13:13) [and again in Exodus 34:20].

notes.he: אפי' בתוך שלשים:
notes.en: Immediately: even within thirty [days].

messages.text: There is no redemption for less than a shekel.

notes.dh: ר' יוסי בר יהודה אמר אין פדייה פחותה משקל
notes.he: ומפרש לקמן מ"ט. וכיון דאין פדיה פחות משקל ופטר חמור אינו שוה אלא שקל ליכא דביני ביני ואינה מקודשת:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: there is no redemption for less than a shekel; and below it explains the reason. And since there is no redemption for less than a shekel, and the firstborn donkey is worth only a shekel, there is no difference, and she is not betrothed.

messages.text: The Master said that the verse: “You shall redeem,” teaches that you shall redeem it immediately, and you shall redeem it for any amount. Isn’t it obvious? Why is it necessary to derive these halakhot from the verse?

notes.he: אמר מר תפדה וכו' פשיטא דלא כתיב ביה לא מבן חדש ולא כתיב דמים בשה:
notes.en: The Master said: “You shall redeem,” etc.: obvious, for neither “from a month old” is written about it, nor is any value written for the lamb.

messages.text: It was necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that since the mitzva of redeeming a firstborn donkey is juxtaposed with that of redeeming a woman’s firstborn son in the verse: “Yet you shall redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of non-kosher animals you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:15),

verse.he: כׇּל־פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לְכׇל־בָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ אַךְ ׀ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֵת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר־הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: The first [male] issue of the womb of every being, human or animal, that is offered to GOD, shall be yours; but you shall have the first-born of human beings redeemed, and you shall also have the firstling of impure animals redeemed.

notes.he: דכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו) את בכור האדם ואת בכור הבהמה טמאה תפדה:
notes.en: It is juxtaposed with a firstborn of man: as it is written (Numbers 18:15), “The firstborn of man and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem.”

notes.he: לתנא למימר הואיל ואיתקש לבכור אדם דכתיב אך פדה תפדה את בכור האדם ואת בכור הבהמה הטמאה תפדה:
notes.en: It was necessary for the tanna to say this, since it is juxtaposed with a firstborn of man, as it is written: “But you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem.”

messages.text: it should be inferred that just as a woman’s firstborn son is redeemed after the baby is thirty days old and involves giving the monetary value of five sela to a priest, as stated in the next verse: “And their redemption-money, from a month old you shall redeem them, it shall be, according to your valuation, five shekels of silver” (Numbers 18:16), this firstborn donkey too should be redeemed after it is thirty days old, and a lamb whose value is at least five sela should be given to the priest.

verse.he: וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃
verse.en: Take as their redemption price, from the age of one month up, the money equivalent of five shekels by the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs.

notes.en: Just as a firstborn of man: his redemption is after thirty days, “And their redemption money, from a month old you shall redeem,” and one must give five sela.

notes.en: Just as a firstborn of man is after thirty: as it is written, “And their redemption, from a month old you shall redeem,” and five shekels is his redemption.

messages.text: Therefore, the baraita teaches us: “You shall redeem,” indicating that the redemption of the donkey must be done immediately after its birth, and that you shall redeem it for any amount.

The baraita also states that Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: There is no redemption for less than a shekel. Whichever way you look at it, this statement is difficult: If Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda holds that the verse compares a firstborn donkey to a woman’s firstborn son, he should require a lamb worth five sela, and if the verse does not compare them, from where does Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda derive that a lamb worth a shekel is necessary?

The verse states with regard to redemption of consecrated property: “And all your valuations shall be with the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25), which indicates that all valuations that you assess should not be less than the value of a shekel.

verse.he: וְכׇל־עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁקֶל׃
verse.en: All assessments shall be by the sanctuary weight, the shekel being twenty gerahs.

notes.he: כלו' כל פדיון שאתה פודה:
notes.en: All valuations: that is, every redemption that you redeem.

messages.text: And the Rabbis who disagree with him hold that that verse …

notes.he: ורבנן ההוא וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל בהשג יד הוא דכתיב כלומר עני שאמר ערך פלוני עלי אם יש לו השג יד ליתן שקל חייב ליתנו לכהן דכתיב על פי אשר תשיג יד הנודר ואם אין לו השג יד ליתן שקל פטור משום שנאמר וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל ולעולם גבי פטר חמור תפדה בכל שהוא:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: that [verse], “And all your valuations shall be by the shekel,” is written about affordability; that is, a poor man who said, “The valuation of so-and-so is upon me”: if he can afford to give a shekel, he must give it to the priest, as it is written, “According to what the vower can afford”; and if he cannot afford to give a shekel, he is exempt, because it is stated, “And all your valuations shall be by the shekel.” And actually, regarding a firstborn donkey, “you shall redeem” with any amount.

messages.text: Continued on 11a: the Rabbis read this verse as written with regard to affordability, when one who vowed a valuation cannot pay it in full.
